Here’s a concise factual research note on the restoration of the main hall of Shuri Castle (Seiden), based on primary and independent sources:

---

**Event Overview**

- On October 31, 2019, a fire destroyed Shuri Castle’s main hall (Seiden) along with eight other buildings at the castle in Naha, Okinawa. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))  
- The restoration of the main hall was officially *completed in September 2026*. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))  

---

**Public Reopening**

- A government‐hosted ceremony marked the completion of the restoration work on **November 22, 2026**. ([japantimes.co.jp](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/06/02/japan/okinawa-shuri-castle-ceremony/?utm_source=openai))  
- The main hall is scheduled to open to the public on **November 23, 2026**. Admission to the interior requires advance reservation. ([japan-guide.com](https://www.japan-guide.com/news/shuri-castle-reopening.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

**Restoration Details & Features**

- The reconstruction began in **November 2022**, under a full‐scale project led by the national and Okinawa prefectural governments. ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Total cost of the restoration is about **¥12 billion**. Approximately **¥6.1–6.2 billion** of that has been raised via donations by September 2026. ([proxy.goincop1.workers.dev](https://proxy.goincop1.workers.dev/https/www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/17054077?utm_source=openai))  

- The restored main hall is a three‐story wooden structure. Historical materials and decorative features were closely referenced: vibrant colors believed authentic to the Ryukyu Kingdom period were reproduced, including use of “Kushimagiri Bengara,” a natural iron‐derived pigment from northern Okinawa. ([proxy.goincop1.workers.dev](https://proxy.goincop1.workers.dev/https/www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/17054077?utm_source=openai))  
- Some elements were modified based on newly interpreted historical documents—e.g. a large plaque behind the second‐floor throne changed from vermillion to yellow, and gilded dragon motifs are now sculptures rather than paintings. ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

**Safety, Fire Prevention & Operational Details**

- Strengthened fire prevention was built in: sprinklers and flame detectors (both new), upgraded fire doors, and compact indoor fire hydrants operable by one person. ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai))  
- To ensure safety and prevent overtourism, visitor numbers inside the hall will be limited, and reservations will be required for interior access. ([japan-guide.com](https://www.japan-guide.com/news/shuri-castle-reopening.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

**Primary and Independent Sources**

- **Primary sources** include:
  - Okinawa prefectural government / Cabinet Office announcements. ([japantimes.co.jp](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/06/02/japan/okinawa-shuri-castle-ceremony/?utm_source=openai))  
  - The Okinawa Churashima Foundation, which manages Shurijo Castle Park. ([japan-guide.com](https://www.japan-guide.com/news/shuri-castle-reopening.html?utm_source=openai))  

- **Independent media** confirming these facts include:
  - Nippon TV NEWS 24 Japan ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai))  
  - Jiji Press / Nippon.com ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))  
  - Asahi Shimbun ([proxy.goincop1.workers.dev](https://proxy.goincop1.workers.dev/https/www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/17054077?utm_source=openai))  

---

**Conclusion: Completed Outcome**

This event reflects a *measured outcome* rather than an announcement or plan: the main hall has been **restored**, the restoration is **completed (as of September 2026)**, and the hall will be **open to the public** starting November 23, 2026. All major components—structure, interior decoration, fire safety—have been addressed in this restoration.

Here is a factual research note on the reported event “Firefighters rescue 12 people during apartment fire” in Russia, based on live sources:

---

## What Happened

- The incident took place in **Shchelkovo**, a town in the Moscow Region (Подмосковье), specifically in a five-storey residential building at **4 Belyaev Street**. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  
- Fire broke out in two apartments on the **first floor** of the building. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  
- The alarm was received at **18:56 local time**. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Rescue and Response

- Firefighters rescued **twelve people** in total, of whom **four were children** and eight were adults. ([eia.media](https://eia.media/en/article/incidents/v-podmoskove-pozharnye-spasli-12-chelovek-vklyuchaya-chetyrekh-detey?utm_source=openai))  
- In particular, a woman and her two children were trapped in a third-floor apartment; firefighters forced open a door and evacuated residents via stairwells using rescue devices. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  
- The fire was contained to an area of **40 square meters** and was fully extinguished. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Aftermath & Casualties

- All rescued people were examined by emergency medical services; there were **no confirmed injuries**. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  
- The response involved **41 personnel** and **12 units of firefighting/rescue equipment**. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Sources

- The **primary source** is the press service of the Main Directorate of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations (МЧС) for Moscow Region, which provided the details on the rescue, numbers of people involved, time, and location. ([riamo.ru](https://riamo.ru/news/proisshestviya/v-podmoskove-ognebortsy-spasli-12-chelovek-pri-pozhare-v-dome/?utm_source=openai))  
- Independent confirmation comes from **MK (Moskovsky Komsomolets)** and **EIA.media**, which broadly repeat the same details. ([mk.ru](https://www.mk.ru/incident/2026/11/22/v-podmoskove-pozharnye-spasli-12-chelovek-vklyuchaya-chetyrekh-detey.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Status: Completed Outcome

This is a completed event with verified rescue outcome: 12 people, including 4 children, were safely evacuated, and the fire was extinguished. There is **no indication** of future or planned actions, pledges, or unverifiable injury counts—it is an actual rescue incident with measurable outcome.  

---

Let me know if you want maps, photos, or any official or government reports in full text for archival purposes.

stories.research_notes:
Here is a factual research note on the claims “China reduces pollutants and plans renewable energy revolution,” based on recent primary and independent sources:

---

## What China Has Already Achieved

1. **Pollutant reductions under the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-2025)**  
   - Implementation of ~24,000 ecological/environmental treatment projects. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202601/28/content_WS697a013dc6d00ca5f9a08cf9.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Nitrogen oxides cut by ≈210,000 tonnes; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) by ≈220,000 tonnes. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202601/28/content_WS697a013dc6d00ca5f9a08cf9.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Reduction in chemical oxygen demand by about 3.2 million tonnes; ammonia nitrogen by about 350,000 tonnes. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202601/28/content_WS697a013dc6d00ca5f9a08cf9.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Rural domestic sewage treatment rate rose to ~55% by end-2025, roughly double the rate in 2020. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202601/28/content_WS697a013dc6d00ca5f9a08cf9.html?utm_source=openai))  

2. **Air and water quality improvements in 2026**  
   - From January to July 2026, the nationwide average PM2.5 concentration fell by ≈1.8 μg/m³ (≈6.2%) compared to same period in 2025. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202608/13/content_WS6a7d6b4bc6d00ca5f9a0c991.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - The share of monitored surface-water sections graded Class I to III rose to 86.5%, up ≈2.4 points year-on-year. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202608/13/content_WS6a7d6b4bc6d00ca5f9a0c991.html?utm_source=openai))  

3. **Renewable energy and greenhouse-gas metrics**  
   - By mid-2026, total installed renewable power capacity reached ~2,455 GW (i.e. gigawatts), making up about 60.7% of all power-generation capacity nationwide. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202610/21/content_WS6ad865e6c6d00ca5f9a0ddec.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Solar photovoltaic capacity exceeded coal power capacity in China for the first time (by installed capacity) by end of July 2026. ([english.mee.gov.cn](https://english.mee.gov.cn/Resources/Reports/reports/202611/P020261109729492239703.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
   - Carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP in 2025 fell by about 17.7% compared with 2020; non-fossil fuels accounted for ~21.7% of total energy consumption. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202610/21/content_WS6ad865e6c6d00ca5f9a0ddec.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Planned Targets and Commitments (Announced, Not Yet Fully Completed)

1. **15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) renewable energy goals** (NEA / NDRC)  
   - Total renewable energy consumption expected to reach ~1.8 billion tonnes of standard coal equivalent by 2030. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202607/23/content_WS6a617ed3c6d00ca5f9a0c5e8.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Total installed renewable generation capacity by 2030: about 3.5 billion kW (3,500 GW), with annual generation of ~6 trillion kWh. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202607/23/content_WS6a617ed3c6d00ca5f9a0c5e8.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Combined wind + solar capacity to exceed ~2.8 billion kW, annual output from those to surpass ~4 trillion kWh. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202607/23/content_WS6a617ed3c6d00ca5f9a0c5e8.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Targets for growth: solar thermal, marine energy capacity, pumped-storage, hydropower, etc. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202607/23/content_WS6a617ed3c6d00ca5f9a0c5e8.html?utm_source=openai))  

2. **Three-year Action Plan for Energy Sector Carbon Reduction (2026-2028)**  
   - Annual increase of ~1 percentage point in share of non-fossil energy consumption. ([english.scio.gov.cn](https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2026-07/13/content_118595896.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Raise share of coal power capacity that meets current efficiency benchmarks by 15 points. ([english.scio.gov.cn](https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2026-07/13/content_118595896.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Promote clean energy use in transportation, construction; support zero-carbon industrial parks. ([english.scio.gov.cn](https://english.scio.gov.cn/pressroom/2026-07/13/content_118595896.html?utm_source=openai))  

3. **Other announced policy shifts**  
   - In March 2026, China set a target under its “dual carbon control” framework: reduce carbon emissions per unit of GDP by 17% over the 2026-2030 period compared to 2025. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202610/21/content_WS6ad865e6c6d00ca5f9a0ddec.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - Additional emissions intensity reduction goal for 2026: ~3.8% compared to the previous year. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/china-plans-to-cut-carbon-dioxide-emissions-per-unit-of-gdp-by-around-3-8-in-2026-ce7e5fdadf81fe23?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Independent Verification and Context

- Independent reporting confirms many of the above, for example that solar capacity overtook coal in installed capacity, which is cited in both government source and independent outlets. ([english.mee.gov.cn](https://english.mee.gov.cn/Resources/Reports/reports/202611/P020261109729492239703.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- Analysts note that although pollutant emissions and carbon‐intensity have fallen, China has not yet committed to an absolute cap on total emissions before 2030. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/china-plans-to-cut-carbon-dioxide-emissions-per-unit-of-gdp-by-around-3-8-in-2026-ce7e5fdadf81fe23?utm_source=openai))  
- Some environmental groups suggest that the scale of planned reductions may not be sufficient to meet Paris Agreement obligations, given economic growth expectations. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/china-plans-to-cut-carbon-dioxide-emissions-per-unit-of-gdp-by-around-3-8-in-2026-ce7e5fdadf81fe23?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What the Candidate Headline Overstates or Omits

- The phrase “revolution” is more aspirational: many plans and targets remain in implementation phase, not yet fully realized.  
- “China reduces pollutants” is accurate in many dimensions (NOx, VOCs, sewage, PM2.5), though reductions are relative (e.g., per GDP, or relative to previous periods), not necessarily reducing total national emissions of all pollutants.  
- The claims about renewable energy are supported by concrete progress (solar overtaking coal, large installed renewable capacity) but many large targets are still set for 2030 and beyond.

---

If you want, I can also check if this G1 article was accurately translated from a Brazilian source or just copied from official Xinhua/Government releases. Would you prefer that?

stories.research_notes:
Here is a concise fact-based research note on the status of the Main Hall (“Seiden”) of Shuri Castle in Okinawa as of **November 22, 2026**, based on original/primary sources and independent reports.

---

## What Actually Happened

1. **Fire damage in 2019**  
   - Early hours of October 31, 2019: a fire destroyed the Main Hall (Seiden) of Shuri Castle, along with eight other buildings on the complex. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))

2. **Restoration timeline**  
   - Full restoration of the Main Hall began in **November 2022**. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))  
   - The exterior restoration (the outer ‘look’ of the building) was completed in **July 2025**. ([japantimes.co.jp](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2025/10/31/japan/shuri-castle-reconstruction/?utm_source=openai))

3. **Completion of restoration**  
   - Restoration work on the Seiden’s main hall was **completed in September 2026**, including structural and exterior features. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))  
   - Interior decoration, fire safety systems, guide plaques, and other finishing work followed. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))

4. **Completion ceremony and opening to the public**  
   - On **November 22, 2026**, a Japanese government–sponsored completion ceremony was held to mark the restoration’s official finish. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/57836?utm_source=openai))  
   - Public openings: the Main Hall will be open to the public starting **November 23, 2026**. Advance reservations required for interior tours. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/57836?utm_source=openai))

---

## Architectural, Cultural & Safety Features

- The restoration incorporated findings from historical research to make some design elements more faithful than during previous restoration (1992). Examples include color changes (e.g. using yellow instead of vermilion behind a tablet behind the throne), the recreation of dragon motifs as carvings rather than paintings. ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Fire safety features strengthened: addition of sprinklers, flame and smoke detectors, fire doors, and an automatic alert system tied to local fire authorities. ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai))

---

## Financial & Donation Data

- Total cost of restoration estimated at approximately **¥12 billion** (≈ US$75 million). ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))  
- Donations from domestic and international supporters reached around **¥6.1 to ¥6.2 billion** by end-September 2026, used for interior decoration and preserving artisan techniques. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai))

---

## What Is Still Pending / Not Yet Completed

- While the main hall is now finished, **other outlying structures** destroyed or damaged in the 2019 fire—including the North Hall, South Hall, and companion flanking buildings—have **not yet been fully restored**. No comprehensive schedule has been announced for the restoration of those. ([japan-guide.com](https://www.japan-guide.com/news/shuri-castle-reopening.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Exterior courtyard in front of the hall remains closed for restoration as of mid 2026. ([japan-guide.com](https://www.japan-guide.com/news/shuri-castle-reopening.html?utm_source=openai))

---

## Sources

- Primary / official confirmation: Nippon.com article “(Update) Main Hall of Okinawa’s Shuri Castle Restored 7 Yrs after Fire” by Jiji Press, November 22, 2026. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/57836?utm_source=openai))  
- Independent media coverage: Nippon TV NEWS 24 Japan, The Japan Times, Asahi Shimbun, Mainichi, etc. ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai))

---

## Summary of Measured Outcome vs. Plans / Announcements

| Aspect | Completed / Measured Outcome | Still Planned or Announcement |
|---|---|---|
| Exterior and structural restoration of Main Hall | ✅ Completed Sept 2026; Exteriors visible by July 2025. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/56698?utm_source=openai)) | — |
| Interior decoration, fire-prevention systems | ✅ Installed by Nov 2026. ([nippon.com](https://www.nippon.com/en/articles/-/57836?utm_source=openai)) | — |
| Public opening of main hall interior | ✅ Opens Nov 23, 2026. ([ntv.co.jp](https://www.ntv.co.jp/englishnews/articles/20216ek89k6w3rnfor73.html?utm_source=openai)) | — |
| Restoration of other destroyed buildings on site | — | Restoration planned; schedule not fully determined. ([japan-guide.com](https://www.japan-guide.com/news/shuri-castle-reopening.html?utm_source=openai)) |

---

Overall, the restoration of the Seiden (Main Hall) of Shuri Castle is now complete as of **September 2026**, formally marked on **November 22, 2026**, and opened to the public from **November 23, 2026**. This is a completed outcome, not merely a plan or pledge. Other castle buildings still await reconstruction.
